node.title: Re^3: convert c# to perl code
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
when i run the code above on the string "7512" i get: cA5YjDeU2fOJwwnVFPCuAw==

Apparently, [https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.text.unicodeencoding|UnicodeEncoding] encodes to UTF-16LE - at least that's what your sample seems to show. So in Perl, you'll have to use the [doc://Encode] module for that, and then either use md5_base64 from [doc://Digest::MD5], which removes the padding at the end of the string (==), or, if you want the padding, you'll have to use [doc://MIME::Base64] separately:

use warnings; use strict; use Encode qw/encode/; use Digest::MD5 qw/md5/; use MIME::Base64 qw/encode_base64/; my $string = "7512"; my $md5b64 = encode_base64( md5( encode( 'UTF-16LE', $string, Encode::FB_CROAK|Encode::LEAVE_SRC ) ), "" ); print "Generated String is: MD5:$md5b64\n"; my $expect = "cA5YjDeU2fOJwwnVFPCuAw=="; print $md5b64 eq $expect ? "Matches!\n" : "Doesn't match!\n"; __END__ Generated String is: MD5:cA5YjDeU2fOJwwnVFPCuAw== Matches!
